_comment: THE FILES LISTED HERE ARE KOTVA'S, NOT PIER'S. DO NOT EDIT THEM IN THIS REPO.
They are the substrate protocol modules of the `kotva-client` package, carved out
of this SDK because chunkProof.js was a second implementation of a kotva spec
section (substrate/FEEDS.md 5.3) living in a product. Their source of truth is
kotva/bindings/js/src; scripts/check-kotva-parity.mjs fails the test run if a
byte here drifts from the hash recorded for it below.
A fix belongs UPSTREAM: change it in kotva, cut a new bindings/js tag, then run
`npm run kotva:pin -- ../../kotva` to re-sync and re-pin. Editing the copy here
is the exact drift this pin exists to prevent.
MIXED PROVENANCE (as of the ts-migration-2 branch). `tag`/`commit`/`version`
below are kotva's last FORMALLY TAGGED bindings/js release and cover
signaling.js and rendezvousSignaling.js unchanged. The other six files --
errors.ts, secureTransport.ts, relayBox.ts, chunkProof.ts, prekeys.ts,
rendezvous.ts -- were advanced past that tag to kotva `main` @
9485b127116cf28a9379063049c08a65eed896d4 ("Merge fix: b64urlEncode silently
corrupted non-Uint8Array views", merging 46c0a06 "bindings/js: widen
b64urlEncode to correctly handle any ArrayBufferView" + cc270a3 test coverage).
Previously advanced to 1a2f0711ebfb844dd27b33e9d1918f09a666b763 ("convert
kotva-client to TypeScript", type-level only). Re-synced 2026-08-05: of the six
advanced files, only rendezvous.ts changed between those two commits -- a real
data-corruption fix, not drift. b64urlEncode mishandled any ArrayBufferView
that was not a plain Uint8Array (a non-1-byte-per-element TypedArray like
Int16Array underwent an element-wise numeric conversion instead of a
byte-for-byte reinterpretation, producing wrong length/values; a DataView
produced zero bytes -- silent total data loss). Reachable only from untyped
JS callers: the declared parameter type was narrower than the runtime
`ArrayBuffer.isView()` guard in `_deposit`, so a plain-JS caller passing e.g. a
DataView slipped past the type system and got silently corrupt bytes on the
wire. errors.ts, secureTransport.ts, relayBox.ts, chunkProof.ts, prekeys.ts are
byte-identical to the prior sync -- verified, not assumed. No new bindings/js/vX
tag has been cut for the current commit yet -- re-pin all eight uniformly once
one exists.
WHY signaling.js / rendezvousSignaling.js were NOT advanced: kotva's
signaling.ts types `SignalPayload.type` as the closed union
'offer'|'answer'|'ice'|'join'|'leave' and `signal()`'s `toId` as `string`
(no null), and defines no `data`/`identity` fields on SignalPayload, and
names the prekey-claim shape `SignedPreKeyClaim`. pier's own
call/fabricSignaling.ts (a real, already-TypeScript consumer, not test code)
sends arbitrary app-level kinds ('join', 'sdp', 'screen-share', ...), passes
`toId: null` for broadcast, and threads `data`/`identity` through the same
envelope -- and pier's own fabric.ts imports the type under the name
`SignedPreKeyAnnouncement`. Verified empirically: swapping in kotva's
signaling.ts + rendezvousSignaling.ts verbatim produces 10 tsc errors in
fabric.ts and call/fabricSignaling.ts (TS2345/TS2339/TS2353/TS2305/TS2322).
This is a real, load-bearing protocol-surface divergence, not drift, and not
safe to resolve unilaterally mid-migration -- it needs a human decision:
either widen kotva's core signaling types upstream, or split pier's copy
into a small pier-owned extension layer wrapping a byte-pinned kotva core.
Until then these two stay JS + hand-written .d.ts sidecar, still pinned to
the original tag below, and are NOT byte-identical to kotva `main`.
This is an INTERIM mechanism, not the intended end state. The end state is an
ordinary version-pinned dependency on `kotva-client`. It is not one today for a
concrete, verified reason: npm has no subdirectory support for git dependencies
(npm 11.6.2 clones the repo and reads package.json at the CLONE ROOT, which for
kotva does not exist), so the Cargo tag-pin convention this repo uses for
kotva-core -- { git = "...kotva", tag = "core-v0.2.0" } -- has no npm equivalent.
See README.md 'Consuming kotva-client' for the one-line switch and what unblocks it.
A path dependency on a sibling ../kotva checkout was deliberately NOT used: this
repo already records what that costs, in crates/pier-cli/Cargo.toml, where the
kotva-depot path dep makes `cargo build` at the root require the sibling. The
hashes below make this gate self-contained instead -- it needs no kotva checkout
and no network, so it runs in CI exactly as it runs offline.
